paper_title: RE-Completeness of Entangled Constraint Satisfaction Problems
authors: Eric Culf (University of Waterloo, Canada), Kieran Mastel (University of Waterloo, Canada)
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 16
statement: It remains open whether non-boolean TVF CSPs, except for 3-colouring, are also RE-complete. As an important example, we do not know if k-colouring for k ≥ 4 is RE-complete with entanglement. However, we do know that any 2-CSP that contains an empty constraint (where all assignments are accepted), such as the language of all 2-CSPs over Zk , is REcomplete as it is not TVF. For RE-complete entangled CSPs, it also holds that SuccinctCSPc−c (Γ)∗1,s is RE-complete, which we show using a mapping between the constraint-variable and constraintconstraint algebras given in Proposition IX.1. This is in contrast with Lemma III.8, where the defect can scale very badly when mapping to the constraint-constraint algebra. Corollary IV.15. Let Γ be a set of constraints satisfying the conditions of Theorem IV.14. Then, there exists a constant s ∈ [0, 1) such that SuccinctCSPc−c (Γ)∗1,s is RE-complete. For some CSPs, we can also show a similar RE-hardness result for the assignment algebra via an oracularisability property. For 2-CSPs, this corresponds to the associated 2-CS game. Corollary IV.16. Let Γ be a set of constraints over Zk such that CSP(Γ)1,1  is NP-complete, and Γ is boolean TVF, Γ = {̸=Z3 }, or Γ = C ⊆ Z2k . Then, there exists a constant s ∈ [0, 1) such that SuccinctCSPa (Γ)∗1,s is RE-complete. More generally, the hardness extends to the assignment algebra with commutation.

There is a perfect zero knowledge CSMIP∗ (2, 1, 1, s) protocol for the halting problem in which the soundness parameter s is constant, the questions have length poly(n) and the answers have constant length. Furthermore, if a game in the protocol has a perfect strategy, then it has a perfect synchronous quantum strategy. Corollary IV.17. Let Γ be a set of constraints satisfying the conditions of Theorem IV.14. Then, there exists a constant s ∈ [0, 1) such that SuccinctCSPa+comm (Γ)∗1,s is RE-complete. This follows immediately from the mappings between the constraint-variable and assignment with commutation algebras given in Lemmas III.9 and III.10. By these, the values of the defects for these algebras are equal up to constant factors (for constraint systems with constant-size constraints and alphabets) and therefore hardness of deciding one directly implies hardness of the other. Next, as noted in the introduction, we can extend the undecidability of entangled CSP languages to non-succinct languages, by considering computable reductions that are not polynomial-time.
